questions.q: What does `az deployment group what-if` do?
options: Previews exactly what a deployment would create, modify, or delete, without applying any of it
Immediately applies the deployment and then asks whether to keep it
Only works against ARM JSON templates, never against Bicep files
Deletes every resource in the resource group not in the template
questions.explain: what-if evaluates the template against the resource group's current state and lists the changes, the same role terraform plan plays before terraform apply.

questions.q: In a what-if result, what does the `~` symbol mean?
options: The resource would be modified in place
The resource is unaffected by the deployment
The resource would be created for the first time
The resource would be deleted
questions.explain: ~ marks an in-place modification, the same meaning Terraform's own plan output gives the tilde symbol.

questions.q: Why doesn't Azure's default incremental deployment mode delete a resource removed from the template?
options: Incremental mode only adds and updates resources present in the template — it never removes what's no longer there
Incremental mode always deletes every resource not explicitly protected
Deleting resources is only possible through the Azure Portal, never through a deployment
Incremental mode requires manual confirmation for every delete, which this lesson didn't cover
questions.explain: Incremental mode is additive/updating only; a resource removed from the template is simply left alone, orphaned from anything still managing it.

questions.q: What real problem does ARM's complete mode have as a fix for that gap?
options: It is slower than incremental mode but otherwise identical
It only works with .bicepparam files, not JSON parameter files
It cannot be run through the Azure CLI, only the Portal
It deletes anything in the resource group not present in the template, including resources the deployment never created
questions.explain: Complete mode deletes everything unmanaged in the resource group, not just what a given deployment previously created — dangerous at resource-group scope.

questions.q: What does `--action-on-unmanage deleteResources` do on a Deployment Stack?
options: Prevents the stack from ever being updated again
Deletes the specific resources the stack no longer manages, such as ones removed from the template
Only applies when the stack itself is deleted, never on a template update
Deletes the entire resource group whenever the template changes
questions.explain: deleteResources cleans up exactly the resources the stack is no longer managing, whether that's from a template update or from deleting the stack itself.
